cards.text: A letter just came in, friend, and it's from Simon Peter. He signs himself a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ. Servant FIRST, then apostle, so the man had the big title and still led with the apron. He's writing to people who received their faith through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ.

cards.question: Peter tells his readers they received a faith as ___ as ours.

cards.text: Then comes his greeting: "Grace and peace be multiplied to you…" MULTIPLIED, friend, like a batch that doubles every time you open the oven, and I would trade my mustache for that oven… okay, not the mustache, I'd have nothing left to hold the spatula.

cards.question: Peter wants grace and peace multiplied to his readers. Through what?

answers.text: The knowledge of God and of Jesus
The strength of their own effort

cards.text: Now Peter talks about what God's divine power has given us for life and godliness. Hold onto your apron, friend.

cards.question: How much of what we need for life and godliness has God's divine power given us?

answers.text: Most of it with the rest on us

cards.text: And it all comes through knowing Him, the One who called us by His own glory and excellence. That word "knowledge" again, friend, and Peter's not even three verses in.
Through these, He has given us His "precious and magnificent promises." Magnificent, friend. Not the "I'll call you right back" kind of promise. The KEPT kind.

cards.question: Peter says God gave these precious promises for a reason. What is it?

answers.text: So they may share in the divine nature
So they may never face hard times again
So they may be rewarded with great riches

cards.question: Peter says these believers are still waiting to escape the corruption in the world caused by evil desires.

cards.text: Because of all God has given them, Peter writes, "For this very reason, make every effort…" Not snooze-button effort, friend, not "I'll start Monday" effort, EVERY effort.

cards.question: Peter tells his readers to make every effort to add to something they already have. What is it?

cards.text: Step one: to faith, add virtue. Then to virtue, add knowledge.

cards.question: Peter tells his readers to choose one of these qualities and focus on just that one.

cards.text: The stack keeps rising: to knowledge add self-control, then perseverance, then godliness, then brotherly kindness. That box is getting so tall, friend, I need the WHOLE mustache just to carry it.

cards.question: Peter's list climbs one quality at a time. What's the last one he adds, right on top of brotherly kindness?

cards.text: So why stack all that? Peter says if they have these qualities and keep growing in them, it makes a real difference in how they know our Lord Jesus Christ.

cards.question: If they keep growing in these qualities, those qualities will keep them from being ___ and ___ in their knowledge of Jesus.

cards.text: But someone missing these traits? Peter says that person is "nearsighted to the point of blindness." That was me back in the junk drawer, squinting at a takeout menu in the dark for YEARS.

cards.question: Peter says the person missing these traits has forgotten something. What?

answers.text: That he was cleansed from his past sins
That he once promised to follow God
That he still has work to finish

cards.text: So Peter brings it home and calls them brothers: strive to make your calling and election sure. Not "I THINK I turned the oven off" sure, friend, SURE sure.

cards.question: Peter says if they practice these things, they will ___ stumble.
Peter ends with what's waiting for them. What kind of welcome will they receive into the eternal kingdom of Jesus?

cards.text: A lavish reception into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, friend. Take it from a stamper who spent years watching the drawer open and close again: being welcomed IN is a VERY big deal.
